page: Vultr voc-m-32c-256gb-1600s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC processor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with multithreading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled with a 1600 GB NVMe SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core metrics placing in the top 25% of tested instances. Passmark CPU physics tests also rank in the strong tier. However, memory bandwidth benchmarks, including uncached read and write operations, perform in the average range. A notable performance tradeoff is observed in single-threaded gzip compression, which registers in the bottom 25% tier, though multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Redis SET operations maintain average throughput.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers high resource density, combining a substantial memory footprint with dedicated CPU cores and fast local NVMe storage. This balance makes it well-suited for memory-intensive workloads, database hosting, Redis caching layers, and medium-scale data processing tasks. The server is also capable of handling moderate LLM inference workloads, achieving average speeds for prompt processing and text generation on models up to 7B parameters.
